newsitem.title: USA: Colonel who questioned Boorda's medals removes two.
newsitem.headline: Colonel who questioned Boorda's medals removes two.

text.p: A retired army colonel who questioned medals worn by top Navy admiral Jeremy "Mike" Boorda before Boorda killed himself last year wrongly claimed credit for two of his own military awards, television networks reported Thursday.

Boorda killed himself in May 1996 shortly before he was to meet with Newsweek magazine reporters, including Army Col. David Hackworth, to discuss whether he properly wore valour pins on his Vietnam War service ribbons.
But Hackworth, a consultant to Newsweek, has deleted two of his own military awards from a list published on his home page on the Internet, the networks reported.
After questions were raised by veterans, Hackworth removed one of two Distinguished Flying Crosses listed on his home page and an Army Ranger service tab, the reports said.

He sent one of the veterans an e-mail message saying he was awarded the Ranger tab "in error" and "that I have discovered I only have been awarded one" Distinguished Flying Cross instead of the two he listed, CBS said.
He suggested a "sleepy clerk" at army headquarters made the mistake, and insisted there was a fundamental difference between his case and Boorda's, the network reported.
"I didn't make it up," CBS quoted Hackworth as saying. "Not like Boorda."
